title: Websocket hub contract: Cloudflare Durable Objects hibernatable WebSockets shape (scope global, new topic websocketHubContract)
context: A named DO instance can host many websocket clients via state.acceptWebSocket per the hibernatable WebSockets shape (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/). The runtime hibernates the object when idle and wakes it on the next message; the wake handler runs from cold and reads the same storage. This is the shipped answer for the coordinated-multiplayer shape consumers reach for. A future non-Cloudflare hub adapter (a Redis pub-sub broker, a bespoke websocket server) would conflict on the same topic; the guide names the trade.
decision: The shipped v1.0.0 default is a Cloudflare Durable Object hub instance behind the DO facade (env.HUB), realising the hibernatable-WebSocket hub shape per REQ-005 and TAC-3404. The websocketHubContract topic scope is global on this blueprint; the topic string is websocketHubContract. A future non-Cloudflare adapter would contribute the same topic string, forcing a DELIBERATE conflict the operator resolves with a project-level ADR.
consequences: The applying project inherits Cloudflare's documented hibernatable-WebSockets contract, the hibernate-after-idle window (elicited per ADR-3405) and the idempotent wake-handler shape. Standards trace clause: Cloudflare Durable Objects hibernatable WebSockets shape (per https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/). The hub shape shares the DO namespace mechanic with the single-cell shape; a future non-Cloudflare websocket-hub sibling mints on demand and the two-blueprint split conversation resurfaces then.
